cards.prompt: What must a facility have before FDA issues an MQSA certificate?
cards.answer: Accreditation by an FDA-approved accreditation body (and compliance with the § 900.12 quality standards).

cards.prompt: How long does a provisional certificate last, and can it be extended?
cards.answer: Up to 6 months; not renewable; one 90-day extension may be requested.

cards.prompt: How often is a certified facility inspected by an MQSA inspector?
cards.answer: At least annually.

cards.prompt: Which facilities are excluded from MQSA Subpart B facility standards?
cards.answer: Department of Veterans Affairs facilities.

cards.prompt: How often does the accreditation body review clinical images, and what is submitted per unit?
cards.answer: At least every 3 years; CC and MLO views from two examinations per unit.

cards.prompt: Name the eight clinical image review attributes.
cards.answer: Positioning, compression, exposure level, contrast, sharpness, noise, artifacts, examination identification.

cards.prompt: What three areas do the EQUIP inspection questions address?
cards.answer: Ongoing clinical image quality review (sample images per technologist and interpreting physician); corrective action for poor-quality images, with feedback; lead interpreting physician oversight of QA/QC records.

cards.prompt: What is MQSA's general requirement for a technologist?
cards.answer: State license for general radiography, or general certification from an FDA-recognized body.

cards.prompt: Initial mammography requirements: how many contact hours, supervised exams, and modality hours?
cards.answer: 40 contact hours; 25 exams under direct supervision; 8 hours in each modality used.

cards.prompt: Define direct supervision for a mammography exam.
cards.answer: The supervisor is present to observe and correct, as needed, the person performing the exam.

cards.prompt: Under MQSA, one CEU equals…
cards.answer: One contact hour of training (an hour of direct instruction).

cards.prompt: Technologist continuing education requirement?
cards.answer: 15 mammography CEUs in 36 months, at least 6 related to each modality used.

cards.prompt: Technologist continuing experience requirement?
cards.answer: 200 mammography exams in 24 months.

cards.prompt: How does a technologist requalify after missing the experience requirement?
cards.answer: Perform at least 25 exams under direct supervision of a qualified technologist before resuming unsupervised exams.

cards.prompt: Training needed before independently using a new mammography modality?
cards.answer: At least 8 hours of CEUs in that modality.

cards.prompt: Which end dates may a facility choose for counting CE and experience windows?
cards.answer: The annual inspection date, the last day of the preceding calendar quarter, or any date in between.

cards.prompt: Interpreting physician continuing requirements (contrast with technologists)?
cards.answer: 960 exams in 24 months; 15 category I CME in 36 months.

cards.prompt: Who has general responsibility for the facility's QA program?
cards.answer: The lead interpreting physician.

cards.prompt: What is the QC technologist responsible for?
cards.answer: All QA tasks not assigned to the lead interpreting physician or the medical physicist (ensuring others who perform them meet requirements).

cards.prompt: Physicist survey: how often, and when is the report due?
cards.answer: At least once a year; report sent within 30 days of the survey.

cards.prompt: When is a mammography equipment evaluation required?
cards.answer: New installation; disassembly and reassembly; major component change or repair (and modality conversion, treated as a new unit). Fix problems before clinical use.

cards.prompt: How long are QC test records kept?
cards.answer: Until the next annual inspection is completed with compliance found, or until the test is done two more times at its frequency, whichever is longer.

cards.prompt: Which assessments make a mammogram 'positive' under MQSA?
cards.answer: Suspicious; Highly Suggestive of Malignancy.

cards.prompt: List the seven MQSA final assessment categories.
cards.answer: Negative; Benign; Probably Benign; Suspicious; Highly Suggestive of Malignancy; Known Biopsy-Proven Malignancy; Post-Procedure Mammogram for Marker Placement.

cards.prompt: After 'Incomplete: Need prior mammograms for comparison', when is a follow-up report due?
cards.answer: Within 30 calendar days of the initial report, whether or not priors are obtained.

cards.prompt: Name the four report density categories in order.
cards.answer: Almost entirely fatty; scattered areas of fibroglandular density; heterogeneously dense (may obscure small masses); extremely dense (lowers sensitivity).

cards.prompt: Lay summary deadlines?
cards.answer: Within 30 calendar days of the exam; within 7 calendar days of final interpretation for Suspicious or Highly Suggestive.

cards.prompt: Provider report deadlines?
cards.answer: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days from the exam; within 7 calendar days of final interpretation for Suspicious or Highly Suggestive.

cards.prompt: Which report density categories map to 'Your breast tissue is dense'?
cards.answer: Heterogeneously dense and extremely dense.

cards.prompt: When did the federal breast density notification requirements take effect?
cards.answer: September 10, 2024.

cards.prompt: List the seven image identification items.
cards.answer: Patient name + additional identifier; exam date; view and laterality (near axilla); facility name and location; technologist ID; cassette/screen ID; unit ID if more than one unit.

cards.prompt: Retention period for original mammograms and reports?
cards.answer: Longest of: at least 5 years; at least 10 years if no additional mammograms at the facility; or State/local law.

cards.prompt: Deadline to transfer originals or release copies on request?
cards.answer: Within 15 calendar days of the request.

cards.prompt: Three minimum outcome audit measures?
cards.answer: Positive predictive value, cancer detection rate (per 1,000), and recall rate.

cards.prompt: How often is outcome audit data reviewed, and by whom?
cards.answer: At least every 12 months, by a designated audit interpreting physician.

cards.prompt: Audit definition of a screening mammogram?
cards.answer: Routine views of an asymptomatic patient.

cards.prompt: How long are serious complaint records kept, and where do unresolved serious complaints go?
cards.answer: At least 3 years; reported to the accreditation body.

cards.prompt: What must the MQSA infection control system specify?
cards.answer: Procedures for cleaning and disinfecting equipment after contact with blood or OPIM, following regulations and manufacturer recommendations, with documentation.

cards.prompt: MQSA phantom dose limit?
cards.answer: 3.0 mGy (0.3 rad) average glandular dose per exposure, single CC view of a phantom simulating a standard breast.

cards.prompt: Define a 'standard breast' under MQSA.
cards.answer: 4.2 cm compressed, 50% glandular and 50% adipose tissue.

cards.prompt: Compression force values in the MQSA compression performance test?
cards.answer: At least 111 N (25 lb); initial power drive maximum between 111 N and 200 N (25–45 lb).

cards.prompt: What QC program applies to FFDM and DBT under MQSA?
cards.answer: Substantially the same as the image receptor manufacturer's program, with the screen-film dose maximum still applying.

cards.prompt: Maximum allowed deflection of a flat compression paddle under compression?
cards.answer: 1.0 cm from parallel.

cards.prompt: Required magnification capability for systems used for magnification?
cards.answer: At least one magnification value between 1.4 and 2.0, with the ability to operate without the grid.
